Net map: 0 = the bottom-right rail, the only node touching GND 7 (stem at x~304 running down from the bottom wire at y~261 to the bars at y~282): it carries the right lead of Inductor 4 (2H), the bottom plate lead of Capacitor 1 (3F) down x~258, and the bottom lead of I-DC 5 (2A). n1 = top-left corner: top lead of Inductor 2 (6H) up x~77 to y~177 and right to the + (left) terminal of V-DC 0 (5V). n2 = the minus (right) terminal of V-DC 0 -> right along y~176 -> T at (149,176) down to the top of Resistor 6 (4 ohm) -> on to the left end of Resistor 3 (2 ohm). n3 = right end of Resistor 3 -> right along y~171-175 through the T at (257,173) where the capacitor column drops away -> right to x~327 -> up/over to the top lead of I-DC 5. n4 = bottom-left rail: bottom lead of Inductor 2 at (77,264) -> right along y~261 -> T at (150,261) with the bottom of Resistor 6 -> right to the left end of Inductor 4.
So the mesh is: 5 V source in series with the 6 H inductor on the left, 4 ohm shunt, 2 ohm series into the 3 F / 2 A node, 2 H in the bottom return, ground taken at the bottom-right rail.
Judgment calls: (a) the two two-terminal parts that sit IN the rails split them - Inductor 4 splits the bottom rail into n4 (left of it) and 0 (right of it), and V-DC 0 splits the top rail into n1 and n2. The bootstrap had shorted Inductor 2 (n1 on both leads) and put Inductor 4's left lead on n1; both are wrong. (b) All four meetings are plain Ts with the branch ending on the through-wire and no hop drawn - (149,176) and (150,261) for Resistor 6, (257,173) and (258,261) for Capacitor 1, plus the GND stem at (304,261) - so all are junctions; verified at 8x, and the top wire is continuous through x=235-300 at pixel level. (c) V-DC 0 is drawn with + on the left and - on the right, so terminal 0 = left (+) = n1, terminal 1 = right (-) = n2. (d) I-DC 5 arrow points up; terminal 0 = top, 1 = bottom. Verticals (Inductor 2, Resistor 6, Capacitor 1, I-DC 5) are listed top-then-bottom, horizontals (Resistor 3, Inductor 4) left-then-right. (e) No off-frame components: all 8 bbox centres are inside the frame and no circuit wire touches a crop edge; the long straight lines at the far left/top/bottom of the scan are notebook rules, not wires.
